data.title: Buy Coca-Cola Stock (KO) to Protect Against Market Volatility, Says UBS
data.description:
Beverage giant Coca-Cola (KO) can help safeguard a portfolio from market volatility, says UBS (UBS). The Swiss bank named its top stock picks that can help to insulate an investor's portfolio from increased volatility as bond yields rise and equity markets sink. And top of the list is Coca-Cola, which offers steady financial results in any type of market as well as a strong dividend payment.

UBS named KO stock its "top pick" in the beverage, household, and personal care category. The bank highlighted the company's quarterly dividend payment of $0.53 per share, giving the stock a healthy yield of 2.39%. In a note to clients, UBS acknowledged that Coke's share price has run nearly 30% this year, but said that the "premium relative to history is warranted given the degree of earnings visibility and upside."

Other Stocks to Buy Now

UBS's recommendation of Coca-Cola's stock comes with U.S. equity markets firmly in the red for September. All the major U.S. indices are firmly in the red on Sept. 15 as the yield on the benchmark 10-year Treasury rises above 5% and hits its highest level since 2007. At the same time, oil prices continue to rise, with Brent crude, the international standard, near $110 a barrel.

data.title: Nvidia Stock (NVDA) Rises on Hospital Adoption of AI Tech
data.description:
Nvidia (NVDA) stock was up 0.6% on Tuesday after the semiconductor and AI company highlighted the use of its open-source AI technology in a children's hospital. The company said that the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP) is using AI and 3D heart models to help doctors plan care for children with rare heart defects.

According to an Nvidia blog post, about 1% of live births involve a congenital heart defect, but each case can have a very different form. CHOP's cardiac modeling service uses MONAI, an open-source medical imaging tool co-founded by Nvidia, to scan exact heart models in seconds. That's worth highlighting, as this work once took a skilled researcher about four hours.

The scanning technology grew from research led by cardiologist Dr. Matthew Jolley, who joined CHOP in 2015. His team helped build SlicerHeart, an open-source tool for viewing and studying 3D medical images. The team then used MONAI Label and Nvidia's Auto3DSeg to train models that can segment heart images with the same level of quality as trained staff. CHOP now uses models before surgery for complex ventricular septal defects, or holes between the heart's lower chambers. In one case, a model helped doctors find a defect after two failed repair attempts.

Nvidia Expects the AI Tech Adoption to Continue to Grow

Nvidia noted that GPU-based tools could cut simulation time from up to four hours, or an overnight run for many options, to near real time. CHOP has started using these tools for closure devices and plans to study their use with transcatheter valves. The work also links SlicerHeart with Nvidia Omniverse and OpenUSD for more advanced heart simulations. The approach is spreading beyond CHOP, as more than 20 children's hospitals in the U.S. now have cardiac modeling programs, while Boston Children's Hospital uses modeling in more than half of its heart surgeries.

CHOP expects about 200 modeled cases this year and plans to apply the tools to other fields through its IDEA Lab. "Open source defies traditional economics for small and heterogenous populations by allowing collaboration and progress without barriers," Jolley said. CHOP pointed out that the shared tools can give small teams access to systems that would otherwise need much larger engineering groups to build and support.

Adoption of Nvidia's technology is a boon to the company, even if it's from open-source programs. That's because it helps create a network that relies on Nvidia's work, increasing demand for its services. That could also lead to more demand for its chips that act as the heart of AI data centers.

data.title: 'Entering the Crucial Phase,' Says Investor About Intel Stock
data.description:
Intel's (NASDAQ:INTC) turnaround efforts have excited investors, but the chip giant is now entering a more demanding phase. The company is making progress on its 14A manufacturing technology, while the rise of agentic AI is creating a powerful new source of demand for CPUs. But the real test now is whether Intel can turn that technical progress and demand into a profitable foundry business.

That matters because Intel's valuation already reflects a substantial recovery in earnings. The company is still losing roughly $2.5 billion a quarter in its foundry operation, yet it trades at a higher earnings multiple compared to several much more profitable chipmakers.

With this in mind, an investor using the pseudonym Quantryon Capital (QC) believes the next stage of the turnaround needs to deliver more than encouraging manufacturing updates: Intel needs external customers, higher shipments and a credible path to foundry profitability.

One of the most important developments is Intel's progress on 14A. The company expects to launch its 0.9 process design kit in October, with Intel's own product teams already designing products around the technology. More importantly, discussions with external customers are moving beyond technology evaluations and toward questions about production capacity. For the investor, that is a meaningful step toward commercialization because it suggests potential customers are considering actual production rather than simply testing Intel's technology.

Risk production is expected in 2027, followed by high-volume manufacturing in 2028. QC sees this as risk reduction, but not yet as a reason for a major revaluation. The next important proof points would be a named external customer, a significant tape-out or a firm capacity commitment.

The investor is also watching Intel's estimates for agentic AI. The company believes these workloads could require four to six times more CPU resources than training, potentially expanding the CPU market as AI inference grows. Intel says server demand is already growing at a double-digit rate, while pricing per core has stabilized.

The problem is that Intel now faces supply constraints rather than a lack of demand. Management expects CPU shortages to persist through 2028. But QC argues that scarcity only creates value if Intel can convert it into more shipments, stronger pricing and better margins. Otherwise, constrained supply simply means lost revenue.

Meanwhile, foundry profitability remains the biggest financial test. Intel is targeting breakeven around the end of 2027, although that could slip into 2028 if additional investment is needed to support new customers. The investor is prepared to accept that delay if it reflects genuine demand. A delay caused by weak utilization, poor yields or unattractive manufacturing economics would be much more damaging.

With Intel trading at roughly 68 times forward non-GAAP earnings and around 25 times forward EV/EBITDA, QC believes the valuation leaves limited room for execution failures. "I now need evidence of commercial traction. External customers, CPU scarcity conversion and packaging economics become more important than another manufacturing milestone," the investor summed up.

To this end, Quantryon Capital rates INTC stock a Hold (i.e., Neutral). (To watch Quantryon Capital's track record, click here)

That is also the conclusion reached by the analyst consensus, a rating based on 23 Holds, 6 Buys and 2 Sells. That said, the $116.5 average price target implies shares will gain 18.5% in the months ahead. (See Intel stock forecast)

data.title: Why Is the Stock Market Down Today, 9/15/26?
data.description:
Both the S&P 500 (SPX) and the Nasdaq 100 (NDX) are in the red on Tuesday, with the former down 0.46% and the latter off 0.44%. Equities are facing pressure from a rising 10-year Treasury yield, which is up 4.7 basis points to 5%, its highest level since 2007. Higher yields increase the opportunity cost of owning stocks and also increase borrowing costs for companies. Furthermore, they reduce the present value of future cash flows. Elevated oil prices have supported yields in recent weeks, with Brent crude oil (BZ) up 2.5% to $108 per barrel.

Fed Decision Looms as Rate Hike Odds Remain High

Meanwhile, the Fed is set to announce its interest rate decision on Wednesday. Traders are pricing in 92.7% odds of a 25-basis-point hike, according to the CME FedWatch tool. Higher rates are generally viewed as a negative for stocks, as they tighten financial conditions and pressure stock valuations.

However, a rate hike may be necessary to support bringing inflation down to the Fed's 2% target. Last Friday, the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) said the Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 3.4% year-over-year in August. The growth was driven by surging gasoline prices and a spike in wireless phone service prices.

data.title: Enova International Stock (ENVA) Plummets Almost 25% on a Failed Acquisition
data.description:
Enova International (ENVA) stock plummeted 24.58% on Tuesday after the technology and analytics company provided an update to its planned purchase of Grasshopper Bancorp. The company has withdrawn its applications with the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency and the Federal Reserve tied to its planned acquisition of Grasshopper Bancorp. Enova International also made the move after a full review of the deal and its path through the bank approval process.

Steve Cunningham, Enova International's CEO, said the company believes pulling the applications is the best choice for Enova and its shareholders. He said bank rules have not kept pace with the credit needs of consumers and small firms that are not well served by banks. Cunningham also said Enova can keep growing without becoming a bank.

What's Next for Enova International?

Enova International reaffirmed its 2026 outlook alongside its acquisition update. The company noted that it expects Q3 revenue to rise about 25% from a year ago, while adjusted EPS is expected to grow about 30%. For the full year, the company still sees revenue growth of 20% to 25% and adjusted EPS growth of 30% to 35%. Enova International said credit and growth trends so far in the quarter support that view.

data.title: Eli Lilly Stock (LLY) Gets New Buy Rating as Weight-Loss Drug Sales Accelerate
data.description:
Wall Street brokerage Berenberg has upgraded Eli Lilly's (LLY) stock to a Buy rating as the pharmaceutical company's weight-loss drug sale steadily accelerate. Kerry Holford, a four-star rated analyst with a 57% success rate, boosted her rating on LLY stock from Hold previously, saying that it sees the drug maker exceeding its 2026 guidance driven by rapid growth of its weight-loss drug sales.

Holford also raised her price target on LLY shares to $1,400 from $1,220. The new price target is nearly 25% higher than where Eli Lilly's stock currently trades. In a note to clients, Holford said that Eli Lilly is now the undisputed market leader when it comes to obesity and diabetes medications. She adds that sales of Eli Lilly's new weight-loss pill called Foundayo, which launched in April of this year, should continue to accelerate in coming months.

Other Reasons to be Bullish on LLY Stock

She added that the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge program, which provides eligible Medicare Part D enrollees access to certain GLP-1 meds for $50 a month, "is fueling a steep uptick in Lilly's obesity drug demand."
